key_insight: Role-prompting changed frontier LLMs’ clinical decisions and ethical priorities, with the insurer perspective most often pushing models away from physician- and patient-aligned recommendations.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare settings, how an LLM is instructed to “take a role” can materially affect whether it recommends or denies complex treatments, so human oversight remains important.
method: Three frontier LLMs tested: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro
Each model answered 25 ethically complex medical cases from physician, patient, and insurer perspectives across 3 runs
Responses were compared with a 6-physician panel using a Patient-Centric Decision Index and ranked ethical values
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 675 total responses and found insurer prompting reduced alignment with physician majority decisions by 50% for GPT-5.4, 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and 10.5% for Opus 4.6 in consensus cases.
watch_item: These results come from simulated case vignettes, so they may not fully capture real-world clinical workflows, local policy, or patient context.
paper_title: Role-Prompting in Frontier Large Language Models Influences Clinical Reasoning in Complex Medical Cases
